input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 is the only right of inspection running against the Company. It meets or exceeds the playbook on notice (30 days' prior written notice, better than the 15-day fallback), timing (Company's normal business hours) and cost (HDI bears its own inspection fees), and it grants no access to Company systems, so it is not in walk-away territory. However, it contains no frequency limit at all, so HDI could inspect repeatedly; frequency is a material term and unlimited audits fail both the preferred (once per 12 months) and the fallback (once per year). The minimal fix inserts a once-per-twelve-month cap. Sub-elements short of preferred but not flagged: inspection is by HDI's General Manager rather than an independent auditor, though the general confidentiality obligation in Section 8.2 binds HDI to protect Company Confidential Information, and there is no underpayment cost-shifting threshold.

proposal.summary: Limit HDI's records inspection right to once per 12 months
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a once-per-twelve-month frequency limit to HDI's inspection right; our playbook allows audits of our records no more than annually. The 30 days' notice, business-hours and HDI-bears-cost terms are acceptable as drafted.

ops.oldText: may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect
ops.newText: may, no more than once in any twelve (12) month period and upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect
